text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S., Israel slam Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, blasting land death penalty.
- Journalist Daoud Kuttab held in Ramallah prison.
- Labour party MP Yossi Beilin: Officers in favour of Lebanon pullout silenced.
- Soldiers seriously hurt by explosion in south Lebanon.
- Dore Gold named Israel's U.N. envoy.
- Scholars scoff at "inflated" Holocaust report.
- Jewish National Fund: Arab real estate purchases prove land-reform plan is bad.
- Strauss-Elite takeover date moved up.
- Tadiran 1st quarter net down 17 percent to $15.5 million.
- El-Op expands sales to South American air forces.
GLOBES
- Assessments: The additional cut in the state budget this year will reach about 900 million shekels.
- Clal and Tnuva examine joint sale of holdings in Hypershuk/Co-Op Zafon.
- Co-Op Blue Square buys Supersol Zafon.
- Strauss and Federman agree on handover of control of Elite will be moved up to start of June.
HAARETZ
- Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister David Levy complete appointments; Gold to U.N. envoy's job.
- U.S. and Israel will discuss findings of U.S. report on Jewish settlements.
- Poll shows a drop in television viewing in Israel.
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: Conditions "cooking" for revival of negotiations with Syria.
- Netanyahu busy or tired, and Treasury is forced to announced: "No decisions taken, discussions will continue."
- Prime minister reprimands cabinet minister Yuli Edelstein for criticism.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak agree: Summit to save peace.
- Hamas group arrested on way to carrying out attacks.
- The first woman pilot of a passenger plane in Israel is 30-year-old Shuli Melman.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu tells Maariv: "I've no esteem for cabinet ministers who throw stones at me."
